I will say the ball activity makes this Jeep extra entertaining, especially for sports fans, as it still offers something fun to do other than driving the car. Fisher-Price Bubble Guppies, Swim-Sational School This is one of those toys that Grandma buys the kid that the kid loves and the mom fantasizes about setting the thing on fire in the back yard. It makes so much noise. It doesn't say one or two phrases, it says a million (okay, that is a hyperbolic statement) phrases. And the kid has their favorite phrase and they switch through the phrases, never letting one complete, until they get to their favorite "tuba fish sandwich!" punchline phrase. So, so, so obnoxious.

It is also geared toward younger kids, but my younger kids have a tendency to pull the slides off and mess them up and then they don't have the ability to fix the problem. So, I hear, "MOM!!!!!" constantly while they are playing with this toy.

I am tired of hearing the "What time is it?" song. You think hearing the cartoon is bad, wait until they can bring the song to life on command. Oy!

The kids like the toy. It is very closed ended. They don't use their imaginations much. But the kids laugh and have some fun. It is not good for multiple kids to play at the same time because it is so closed ended. It is really a one kid at a time toy. If your kid just loves Bubble Guppies, and you love electronic toys- go right ahead.

Grandma- let me give you some advice. Your daughter-in-law will love you if you buy quiet plush Bubble Guppies instead. She'll love you even more if you spring for a nice set of blocks. Unless this toy was specifically asked for, avoid it!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Bubble Guppies, Swim-Sational School

LEGO Star Wars Sith TIE Fighter 75272 Collectible Building Kit, Cool Construction Toy for Kids, New 2020 (470 Pieces) Let’s get the bantha out of the way first, shall we? This new Lego Sith TIE Fighter is priced far too high. The price per brick (ppb) is about 16-17 cents, where in most sets, the ppb is 10 to 12 cents.

The finished build looks sleek, with its red piping edges and new pieces to finish off the points of the wedges. But the ship is small compared to other sets of a similar price, or even compared to previous versions of Lego TIE fighters.

The included minifigs are basic. A generic First Order TIE Pilot, Finn (a duplicate from set 75257), and a Knight of Ren.

I like the build. It’s a ship that actually looks good on display, which is what I do with most of my Lego sets. The build includes a display stand, as the ship can’t stand on its own without perching on the stand.

But I wish there were more details on the cockpit of the TIE, or even more engine details to make it a set more worthy of its high price tag.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture This is a beautiful set, with the vast majority of the pieces being thoughtfully designed and thoughtfully put together. I like that each of the room sets goes together really well, so that you have a cohesive feel throughout your dollhouse without everything feeling identical.

The quality level on some of this is absolutely stunning given that it is at a reasonable price point and made for children. I really love some of the pullout drawers that are actually functional, and the upholstery on the bed and couch, chairs and Ottoman are incredible. I think my favorite piece might be the show off cabinet that has clear plastic windows, so that you can display things in the dollhouse. We have some miniature flower vases and things like that that fit perfectly.

There were a few things that came with the quality a little bit off. The toilet arrived broken, and not only was it broken, but I could tell that the way it was put together facilitated it arriving broken. The toilet seat pins were attached in a way that the toilet seat cannot close properly over the main body of the toilet, and the part that broke off, the back toilet tank, showed very cheap pressboard material underneath, which I did not expect from Melissa and Doug brand. There were a few doors, like the refrigerator, that were also put on a little bit diagonally in a way that would drive type a grown-up a bit crazy.

The vast majority of the things however appeared to be made of real wood and had a really incredible quality and design. I put them into a new dollhouse that I'm creating for fun to play with with my kids, and it's been really fun to accessorize and make everything fit into the dollhouse in a way that feels truly special.

The packaging is ready to be dressed up or wrapped as a gift. The packaging I got was a big, wide, flat cardboard box with a plain brown exterior that you lift the lid and find a bunch of brown paper wrapped furniture. If you wrapped this with wrapping paper, it would be perfect as a gift, but if given right out the box, it definitely lacks a little sparkle. That said, once anybody realizes what is inside, the excitement level of unwrapping each individual piece was kind of like Easter, or Christmas. Really incredible.

Overall I'm really pleased with this set, and so many of these special pieces seem heirloom quality and like things that we will be so happy to continue playing with or keep for grandchildren someday.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture

text_fidelity_a:
Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up We tried this recently on a rainy evening, and it was a fun family activity. However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up

6' Giant Teepee Play House of Pine Wood with Carry Case by Trademark Innovations (White) purchased for my grandsons to use when visiting..... it is large.... large enough for an an adult to get into. The material is a cotton canvas... not terribly thick, but not too thin in my opinion. It was relatively easy to put together... I like that this is a bottom floor attached. It is quite popular to stay grandma's and camp out.... I added some "nap pads" which are perfect for the 5 and 2 year old. I also added a stuffed bear and alligator and a camp lantern that is a lantern or a star map night light. Honestly, I keep it up in the corner of my living room so it is ready for any visit. It does come with a handy bag that has a handle if you'd like to store it when not in use. The poles are wood... a pine I believe... very sturdy. I would recommend this teepee... I always update if there are any issues that may be helpful.
3/25/2016 UPDATE: ...so I just finished deconstructing the teepee and felt an undate with tips might be helpful... first... you will never get the canvas teepee back into the canvas bag provided... it's like folding/rolling a really thick fitted sheet and trying to get into a tube sock.... BUT the wooden poles fit nicely into the canvas bag along with the plastic connector pieces... it would have been nice if the connectors gripped the poles better and stayed connected during the deconstruct phase... however... I just removed all the holed top pieces and then turned the teepee upside down and shook it sort of like a pillow case... the lower pieces eventually come out... I just rolled the teepee up, put all the poles and connector pieces in the bag and set in a large drawer I have. I would have lowered my rating one star for the deconstruct hassle, but honestly, my grandsons love it so much I just can't. The quality is such that this is going to last for many years if we take care of it. It's just a matter of learning how to use it in an efficient manner. Also... I have hard wood floors, so I went to a local carpet store and purchased some carpet padding. I cut into a circle and place it under the teepee when I have it set up... I worry less about bonked heads that way - grandsons 5 years and 2 years. Ok! Hope this is indeed helpful info!

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces THE GOOD:

So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. You can manually check... you are free of bands when you can pop their heads back and split their bodies. If you can't do that, it probably means there are some bands you still need to cut off.

5-Stars!

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?

This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. I'm going to try to find another loom.

I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up Back in the late 1980’s and early 1990’s I used to play MASH in school. No, it had NOTHING to do with the sitcom that some might remember.

The MASH game was an acronym for:

Mansion
Apartment
Shack
House

It was sort of a future/fortune telling game mainly for giggles. The original paper game was of course to tell you what “crush” you ended up with, what kind of “housing” you resided in, what you drove, and how many kids you had. One person drew a circle/swirl, like in this game, and you said STOP to get the “counter” number to begin the fortune telling – crossing off at the count.

This is an updated version of that game, though in all honesty, not near as much fun.

The basic model was to list MASH and three other variables – kids, car – crush. Like this one; you swirled and counted until you came to the end.

This game, while more grown up, is nothing like the old game even with the introduction of “scenarios”. Sadly, this is pretty much paying for something that you can get for free – sometimes you can even add more to the choices – pets, location, job(s) … with the old version, the only limitation is imagination.

This game does pay homage to its origins and includes the ORIGINAL MASH “scenario” card though the choices for everything is left up to the “decks” and not the players’ imaginations. That was, again the entire fun of it.

Depending on exactly what you’re looking for with this game – it might be best to save your money and write it out like I did or look online for MASH game cards. There are really cute printable ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Once I master that - look out! I'd like to make a small lampshade, Christmas ornaments, and focal beads for jewelry.

Just what I need, another hobby!!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player So I played Farkle a long time ago, and my family in another state has begun playing Farkle pretty regularly on family game nights. So I was excited to get Farkle Frenzy. But I have to admit we played the first four games with different rules each time as we figured them out (not sure that I have it completely correct now.) It is definitely not a true form of Farkle, but like I said, it's been a long time, but the scoring definitely is different. Not that that is completely bad. I just can't shake the feeling that I'm getting something wrong.

But as improvement to the game, the shared dice is great, the kids love to depress the bubble and can't wait for their turn to push it. The game board pyramid is also a nice addition in giving them somewhere to place the dice, but the score is difficult and beyond my 6 year old. But we had fun playing it in general and we are looking forward to taking it to Grandma's house where they fully understand Farkle.

Pros
+ Pushing the bubble on the shared dice was a big hit
+ Fast moving game
+ Captured the attention of the boys even if they didn't necessarily understand the scoring.

Cons
- A little confusing on the scoring

Summary
All in all a fun game, even if we are putting a bit of a spin on the game. The 3D game board adds to the interest of young kids and Farkle is a very playable and enjoyable game.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is a fun toy that encourages creativity and keeps kids occupied. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The same is true with this toy. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. The wooden container offers easy storage so that pieces do not get lost and the product's individual pieces are designed to last.

Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is simple yet fun and requires little supervision or explaining. My little princesses like this toy and still find it fun, but I have noticed that it lacks the staying power of some of their favorite toys. Unless I suggest it, they are not likely to use it. They do like it, but I think they have become a little bored with it. They prefer toys with movement and sound, and this offers neither.

This stamp set is certainly durable, but one thing that isn't made to last is the ink pad. I like that the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set comes complete with its own ink and my girls strongly appreciate that the ink is colored purple and pink. However, don't expect the ink to last very long. The small blotches of ink will not offer many stamping adventures, so be prepared to purchase additional ink stamps within a few months.

Although not the perfect toy, the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is nonetheless a good toy for little princesses everywhere. It has many positive qualities, encourages creativity, and is priced right. Like I said, it lacks staying power, but it has enough positive qualities to recommend.

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up Kinetic sand is a fun activity for young kids, like regular sand it has tendency to get all over the place if not contained in a tray or plastic dish but it is easy to clean up and unlike play-doh and other similar modeling toys it doesn't ever dry out. This bake shop set comes with a roller and variety of stamps and molds to make cookies and cupcakes which are all nice quality. I especially like that the molds can fit within the roller for easy storage.

The only downside to this set is that kinetic sand is not really ideal for molding since it has a tendency to flow and collapse if not packed very tightly. Our 5 year old was trying to reproduce some of the cupcake designs shown on the box and was getting frustrated because the sand kept falling apart when she added the icing on top of the cupcake base. I tried to do it myself and was able to reproduce the design but it required packing the sand very tightly and then being very delicate when removing from the molds..

We like kinetic sand, and we like the molds that come with this set but we will probably use them primarily with play-doh instead of kinetic sand because these small molds are kind of difficult for kids to use with kinetic sand. We have some other larger ice cream molds that we have used with kinetic sand in the past, they are easier to use because they are smoother and release the sand without requiring such a delicate touch to prevent it crumbling.
text_fidelity_b: Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game This is a fun game. My boyfriend and I played it. It is only a two-player match game like tic-tac-toe or battleship. The youngest player starts and both players get two cards which they keep face down until the end of the game. The first player pushes out a cube in the top left corner of the game grid. The next player then pushes out another cube on the board with that same cube. The play continues with each player pushing out the next cube with the previous cube just played without using the same grid hole. The idea is to match five of the same characters in a row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. When one player indicates a match, the losing player turns over their cards and if the character on one of the cards matches the winning players match, then that person now wins the game. If there is no match, then the winner keeps his win.

The game is simple, yet fun, and is full of strategy. There are two negatives, however. The game case is difficult to open and it feels like I am going to break off the plastic prongs when I pull it apart. Also, the game wobbles a bit when the outside "wings" are down. Third, it is easy to knock all the cubes out of the game grid. As my boyfriend was playing, he titled the game just a bit to see the characters better and many of the cubes fell out. Other than the lackluster quality of the game parts, the game itself is wonderfully simple and tremendous fun.
text_fidelity_b: DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game
